chapter: Violinists, Stuff Smith and Josh White
title: New Orleans as the supposed jazz centre and early arrangers
summary: He argues that music travelled with troubadours and that arrangers organised bands.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yes. So one guy's in Buffalo. The other guy's in Philadelphia, but the music's all the same because the guy's are traveling, you know, troubadors, and so you take your craft with you, and other people get influenced by it. So the myth of New Orleans music being the jazz center of the world wasn't necessarily so.
Yeah, this is interesting, because in talking to Eddie Barefield, he also brought this up that, you know, talking about this style, that style. He says it was, you know --
It was just music. The bands that had formed didn't have organization until you had people like Don Redman, Fletcher Henderson to write for them. And the
struggling writers without the training that were making arrangements and whatnot because there were always arrangements, you know, somebody had an idea.
But to get it down to its final points, it's now. But now there aren't any of them.
Not too many of them, including me.
